title: Knowledge check: Frontend Authentication and Security Boundaries

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Frontend Authentication and Security Boundaries”?
options: Compile untrusted strings as Vue templates to make them interactive.
Use a hidden frontend button as the only authorization check.
Treat a VITE_ environment variable as secret because it came from .env.
Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.answer_key: Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Frontend Authentication and Security Boundaries directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Authentication state in the UI”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A hidden frontend button enforces authorization.
Color is enough to identify every form error.
Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
Use v-html for all user-supplied strings.
questions.answer_key: Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Authentication state in the UI”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Frontend Authentication and Security Boundaries” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
